description: Arsenic is a chemical element with symbol As and atomic number 33. It is a metalloid and member of group 15, sharing properties with phosphorus and antimony. It occurs naturally in many minerals, usually combined with sulfur and metals, and has various allotropes with the grey form being the most important industrially.
uses: The primary use of arsenic is in alloys of lead for car batteries and ammunition. It is used as an n-type dopant in semiconductor electronic devices and as a component of gallium arsenide. Arsenic and its compounds are used in the production of pesticides, treated wood products, herbicides, and insecticides, though these applications are declining due to recognition of arsenic's toxicity.
characteristics: Grey arsenic has a double-layered structure with interlocked six-membered rings, is brittle with a Mohs hardness of 3.5, and has a high density of 5.73 g/cm³. Yellow arsenic is soft, waxy, and most toxic with a density of 1.97 g/cm³, while black arsenic is glassy, brittle, and a poor electrical conductor. Arsenic sublimes at 887 K (614 °C) at atmospheric pressure and becomes a semimetal that turns into a semiconductor when amorphized.
